Shape-informed cardiac mechanics surrogates in data-scarce regimes via geometric encoding and generative augmentation
desc: High-fidelity computational models of cardiac mechanics provide mechanistic insight into the heart function but are computationally prohibitive for routine clinical use. Surrogate models can accelerate simulations, but generalization across diverse anatomies is challenging, particularly in data-scarce settings. We propose a two-step framework that decouples geometric representation from learning the physics response, to enable shape-informed surrogate modeling under data-scarce conditions. First, a shape model learns a compact latent representation of left ventricular geometries. The learned latent space effectively encodes anatomies and enables synthetic geometries generation for data augmentation. Second, a neural field-based surrogate model, conditioned on this geometric encoding, is trained to predict ventricular displacement under external loading. The proposed architecture performs positional encoding by using universal ventricular coordinates, which improves generalization across diverse anatomies. Geometric variability is encoded using two alternative strategies, which are systematically compared: a PCA-based approach suitable for working with point cloud representations of geometries, and a DeepSDF-based implicit neural representation learned directly from point clouds. Overall, our results, obtained on idealized and patient-specific datasets, show that the proposed approaches allow for accurate predictions and generalization to unseen geometries, and robustness to noisy or sparsely sampled inputs.

title: Effects of Artificial Intelligence Chatbot Interventions on Women during Pregnancy and Postpartum: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
desc: [Healthcare informatics research] Artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots are increasingly used in maternal healthcare to provide real-time, interactive, personalized support. This systematic review and meta-analysis examined the effects of AI chatbot interventions on women during pregnancy and postpartum. PubMed, the Cochrane Library, Embase, the Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature, and the Research Information Sharing System were searched from September 11 to 16, 2025, using the search string "(("Artificial Intelligence"[Mesh] OR "AI"[tiab] OR "Machine Learning"[tiab]) AND ("Chatbot"[tiab] OR "Conversational Agent*"[tiab]) AND ("Pregnancy"[Mesh] OR prenatal[tiab] OR antenatal[tiab] OR postnatal[tiab] OR postpartum[tiab])". Eligible studies were peer-reviewed experimental studies published in English or Korean that evaluated chatbot interventions for women during pregnancy or postpartum. Six studies (four randomized controlled trials and two nonrandomized controlled trials) were included. Intervention themes included gestational diabetes, postpartum depression, well-being, maternal-fetal attachment, aneuploidy testing, and breastfeeding. Individual trials reported improvements in knowledge, self-efficacy, and attachment, as well as reductions in symptoms. The meta-analysis showed no significant effect on depression (estimate = 0.037, p = 0.662) or anxiety (estimate = -0.084, p = 0.279); heterogeneity was low (I² = 0%). AI chatbot interventions show promise for improving maternal knowledge, self-efficacy, and attachment. However, the available evidence does not show consistent reductions in depression or anxiety. Large, rigorously designed studies are needed to refine intervention strategies, ensure equity, and establish a robust basis for integrating these interventions into maternal healthcare systems.

title: From Benchmarks to the Bench: Preference, Correspondence and Selectivity in Bidirectional Drug-Target Screening
desc: Identifying active molecules for known targets and potential targets for existing drugs is central to drug discovery and repurposing. Drug-target interaction (DTI) models can rank vast numbers of drug-target pairs, but limited experimental capacity restricts testing to a small number of candidates. We compared the bidirectional recommendations of 13 released systems across 711 molecular structures of FDA-approved drugs and 614 human proteins. For the same target or drug, pairs of models produced completely disjoint Top-10 molecule and protein lists in 77.8% and 70.1% of comparisons, respectively. Even where recommendations overlapped, agreement between some systems largely reflected recurring preferences for the same candidates. Published inhibition measurements for 79 molecules and 65 kinases revealed that some systems enriched active candidates, yet their hit yields changed little when recommendations were matched to different drugs or targets, whereas other systems lost substantially more hits. Some of the former systems also rarely ranked both molecules and kinases correctly when two drugs favoured different kinases. We further retrained the same architecture on the same data, with the training objective fixed and random seeds varied. Despite similar test performance, mean pairwise Top-10 overlap on a separate screening catalogue was about two candidates. Our study moves DTI model evaluation beyond benchmark performance to assess whether model predictions can guide meaningful experimental decisions in drug discovery and target identification.

title: Using a large language model as the primary coder in health content analysis: a verification framework, per-variable reliability and proposed reporting items.
desc: Objective: To describe and evaluate a framework for using a large language model (LLM) as the primary coder in health content analysis, and to propose reporting items for LLM assisted studies, because no reporting standard exists. Methods: An LLM coded 6,982 Instagram and TikTok posts using a human written, human calibrated instrument. The framework has six components: human authorship of the instrument; two round human calibration; source discipline; quote anchored coding; verification in a representative and an outcome enriched sample, blinded in both directions; and per variable reliability reporting against a prespecified threshold, with the consequence of failure fixed in advance. Agreement was measured with Gwets AC1, prespecified because the outcome distribution was heavily skewed. Results: Agreement between the two human coders on the primary outcome rose from AC1 0.456 to 0.977 after two ambiguous rules were rewritten. LLM human agreement was 0.847 in the representative sample (N = 150) and 0.868 in the enriched sample (N = 50). Five of eight conditional variables fell below the 0.80 threshold and became exploratory: variables asking whether a defined textual feature was present met it, whereas those requiring graded judgement did not. The human coder identified misinformation more often than the LLM, so prevalence estimates are likely underestimates. Agreement on female targeting was lower for self-identified ethnic minority creators (0.744 versus 0.902). Conclusion: LLM coding cannot be computationally reproduced, so its reliability must be shown empirically: per variable agreement with independent human coding, the direction of remaining error, and a prespecified response to shortfall. The authors propose 18 reporting items for LLM assisted content analysis.

title: When Artificial Intelligence Plays It Safe: Large Language Models Preserve Surgical Sensitivity at the Cost of Diagnostic Specificity in Acute Abdominal Pain.
desc: [The American surgeon] BackgroundIn acute abdominal pain, artificial intelligence may appear safe by preserving surgical sensitivity while increasing resource use through reduced specificity. We evaluated this safety-stewardship trade-off across frontier large language models (LLMs) to provide an exploratory diagnostic benchmark.MethodsWe performed a cross-sectional in-silico study using 50 standardized synthetic vignettes (25 urgent surgical, 25 non-urgent) internally developed by our investigative group. GPT-5.5, Claude 4.0 Opus, and Gemini 3.0 Ultra were evaluated using identical zero-shot deterministic prompting against an internally established, blinded dual-specialty expert consensus.ResultsExact primary-diagnosis accuracy was 92.0% (95% CI, 81.2-96.8%) for GPT-5.5, 88.0% (95% CI, 76.2-94.4%) for Claude 4.0 Opus, and 76.0% (95% CI, 62.6-85.7%) for Gemini 3.0 Ultra. Surgical sensitivity remained high across models (84.0% to 96.0%), whereas specificity was lower (64.0% to 80.0%) than specialist consensus. Models demonstrated a conservative escalation pattern with frequent over-triage decisions. Positive likelihood ratios ranged from 2.33 to 4.60. Over-investigation bias was the predominant error pattern.ConclusionIn this exploratory benchmark, frontier LLMs consistently prioritized surgical sensitivity over specificity in internally authored structured acute-abdomen vignettes. These findings reflect differences in performance on controlled synthetic scenarios rather than independently validated clinical diagnostic accuracy. Claims regarding clinical patient safety or readiness for implementation require future prospective validation with independent, real-world clinical cases and external multidisciplinary adjudication.

title: Contactless Estimation of Respiratory Frequency Using 3D-CNN on Thermal Images
desc: Monitoring physiological parameters such as respiratory rate ($f_R$) is essential for diagnosing and managing various pathological conditions. Thermal imaging offers a promising contactless alternative to traditional methods, which often rely on partially invasive sensors or obtrusive wearable systems. However, existing approaches for $f_R$ estimation from thermal signals typically require extensive pre-processing and manual or semi-automatic region-of-interest (ROI) tracking, limiting their practical applicability. This study proposes a deep learning-based method for estimating $f_R$ directly from thermal videos, eliminating the need for complex pre-processing and ROI tracking. A 3D Convolutional Neural Network (3D-CNN) is developed to operate on raw thermal video data. To address challenges related to small datasets, the model is trained using data augmentation and transfer learning from synthetic datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves a validation $R^2$ score of approximately 0.61 on both pre-processed and raw thermal videos. By simplifying the workflow, this method holds promise for enhancing the feasibility of thermal imaging in real-world applications, such as remote healthcare and driver monitoring in automotive applications.

title: Automated Screening for Generalized Anxiety Disorder Using Voice Analysis and Machine Learning
desc: This study evaluated machine learning models for screening elevated generalized anxiety symptoms from remotely collected neutral read speech in 1,788 adults from Botswana, Ghana, Nigeria, and Tanzania. Elevated symptoms were defined by Generalized Anxiety Disorder 7-item (GAD-7) questionnaire scores [≥] 5. Nine classifiers were assessed across nine scenarios defined by speech-task configuration (short sentence, long passage, or both tasks) and sex stratification under participant-separated, repeated nested cross-validation (CV). Acoustic-only models used the extended Geneva Minimalistic Acoustic Parameter Set, and context-augmented models added age, self-reported health, and sex where applicable. With feature selection, the highest mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCROC) was 0.594 for acoustic-only models and 0.699 for context-augmented models, the latter in the female-only combined-task scenario. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) identified fundamental frequency descriptors as prominent acoustic predictors, while health status and age were the leading predictors in context-augmented models. Performance varied across scenarios, and feature selection provided no consistent benefit. Secondary regression poorly estimated continuous symptom severity. These findings indicate limited discrimination from neutral speech acoustics alone and improved performance with participant context, warranting external validation.

title: Deep learning models detect neuromuscular disease and quantify functional impairment from video-derived biomechanics data.
desc: [Research square] Measurements of human movement are critical for evaluating patients with neuromuscular diseases. However, current clinical tools are limited in sensitivity and can fail to detect the full spectrum of movement changes patients may exhibit. These limitations can obscure early signs of decline, delaying interventions that could preserve function and independence. OpenCap--a smartphone application that performs video-based markerless motion capture--can help address this gap by enabling scalable, out-of-lab measurements of human movement. Here, we present a method for both detecting disease and quantifying the severity of impaired movement from smartphone videos of a patient's motion. We used OpenCap to measure kinematics from 337 individuals with diagnoses spanning 12 rare, genetically-defined neuromuscular diseases and 78 age-matched healthy controls. Our dataset is the largest existing publicly available resource of body segment kinematics for this class of diseases. These data were collected in neuromuscular clinics during regular clinic visits as well as at conferences and community events across the United States. We trained deep learning models on these kinematic time series to differentiate between participants with neuromuscular disease and controls (AUROC = 0.97 [0.93-1.00]). We also developed a movement impairment severity score that correlates with both participants' ratings of their own functional abilities (ρ= -0.81, p < 0.001) and existing clinical tests of movement capabilities such as run speed (ρ= -0.83, p < 0.001). Our methods for detecting disease and deriving quantitative biomarkers of movement impairment from smartphone videos have the potential to complement clinical assessments, inform screening protocols, and improve clinical trial endpoints.

title: A Statistical Framework for Training Data Auditing of Large Language Models
desc: Training-data auditing asks whether data of interest were used to train a large language model (LLM), a question central to privacy auditing, copyright protection, and benchmark-contamination detection. These concerns are particularly relevant to the use of copyrighted books and scientific papers in pre-training, as well as synthetic text and medical question-answer records in fine-tuning. In practice, training membership signals may be concentrated in only a few passages of a long document, making it important to aggregate evidence within each document without diluting these localized signals. Beyond individual documents, auditing a target collection requires an overall assessment based on the document-level evidence. In this paper, we propose a unified statistical framework for document-level membership inference, target-collection global auditing, and suspicious-subset identification. We integrate complementary chunk-level membership evidence with Cauchy combination to construct document scores for document-level membership inference. The document scores and their calibrated p-values further enable an overall assessment of training-data collection use and the identification of suspicious documents through multiple testing. Under the stated exchangeability conditions, we establish finite-sample validity of document-level p-values, type-I error control for global auditing, and false discovery rate control for subset identification. Case studies on BookTection, Pile-arXiv, Cosmopedia, and HealthCareMagic demonstrate the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed framework in auditing pre-training and fine-tuning data.

title: Development and Validation of MetaVidence: A No-Code Application for Accessible and Reproducible Meta-analysis
desc: BACKGROUND: Meta-analyses are central to evidence-based medicine, but the R packages that implement current methods require programming skills, and most graphical tools cover only a single study design. Here, we aimed to develop and validate a free no-code application that performs the main forms of meta-analysis within a single interface. METHODS: We developed MetaVidence as a Shiny application built on the meta, metafor, netmeta and lme4 packages, which runs in the browser through WebAssembly and is also available as an R package. Agreement with direct package calls was evaluated across effect measures, models, estimators and secondary analyses, and 12 published meta-analyses were reconstructed. Usability was assessed with the System Usability Scale among researchers who had previously conducted a meta-analysis. RESULTS: MetaVidence performs pairwise, single-arm, pre-calculated, network and diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis through a three-step workflow of data verification, model specification and results. In three of the five families, multiple outcomes can be analyzed in a single run with the same settings, and every analysis reports the parameters that should be described in the methods section. A total of 6,321 validation checks were performed, and the maximum absolute difference in the reference-dataset comparisons was 3.9x10^(-16). The diagnostic module reproduced the anti-CCP example of the Cochrane Handbook to within 0.0002, and all 12 published meta-analyses were reproduced within half of the last reported digit. Fifty-nine researchers rated MetaVidence with a mean System Usability Scale score of 82.8 (95% CI 76.2-89.5). CONCLUSIONS: MetaVidence integrates the main forms of meta-analysis into a single validated interface that does not require programming. These findings support its use as an accessible and reproducible resource for evidence synthesis, particularly for researchers without programming skills or statistical support.

title: Integrative 3D imaging and deep learning approach reveals cardiac fibroblast dynamics after myocardial infarction.
desc: [JCI insight] Cardiac fibroblasts (CFs) are key mediators of heart failure progression, driving fibrotic scar formation after myocardial infarction (MI). Conventional preclinical assessment of MI relies on two-dimensional histology, which cannot resolve the three-dimensional (3D) architecture of the injured heart. Understanding the molecular mechanisms of CF activation is critical for identifying new drug targets, yet spatial mapping of gene expression in intact hearts remains challenging. To address this, we developed a high-throughput imaging pipeline that combined single-cell-resolution gene expression profiling in cleared whole hearts with light-sheet fluorescence microscopy and an AI-driven analysis framework optimized for MI characterization. Using this approach, we mapped expression of periostin (Postn), collagen triple-helix repeat containing 1 (Cthrc1), and asporin (Aspn) - genes associated with CF activation. These markers were detected by day 3 post-infarction in the endocardium and border zone, preceding collagenous scar formation, then expanded across the infarcted myocardium before declining toward baseline during scar maturation. These findings revealed a spatially organized progression of fibrosis-associated gene expression that began in defined regions of the injured heart and subsequently extended throughout the infarcted myocardium. Whole-organ gene-expression imaging combined with deep-learning-based analysis enabled quantitative spatiotemporal mapping of molecular remodeling and provides a framework for investigating disease progression in intact organs.

title: Physics-Informed Deep Learning for Shear Wave Speed Estimation in MR Elastography
desc: Objective: Magnetic Resonance Elastography (MRE) is a non-invasive imaging technique for mapping biomechanical properties of in vivo tissue, including shear wave speed (SWS), but involves intrinsically slow data acquisition and an ill-posed wave inversion. Instead of relying on handcrafted image priors, we propose a data-driven approach jointly combining image reconstruction and MRE inversion for robust SWS estimation from undersampled k-space data. Methods: Our physics-informed reconstruction framework comprises two blocks: a model-based neural network (NN)-regularized reconstruction module and a phase-gradient inversion (k-MDEV) calculating SWS from the reconstructed images. Concatenating both blocks yields an end-to-end trainable method to estimate SWS directly from measured k-space data. We evaluated the method on retrospectively highly undersampled brain MRE data and compared it to a total variation (TV) minimization-based approach. We assessed the impact of end-to-end training (qualitative images and SWS maps as targets) versus pre-training (qualitative images as targets) and applied the method also to in vivo data. Results: Our approach significantly reduces NRMSE by 30% compared to TV. End-to-end training improves SWS estimation over separate image reconstruction and SWS calculation. Conclusion: Accurate SWS quantification is possible at acceleration factors up to 19. Our method significantly outperforms TV, highlighting the need for data-driven regularization in this challenging MR problem. Further, our approach successfully generalizes to in vivo data. Significance: We present the first end-to-end trainable MRE reconstruction method for estimating SWS maps directly from k-space. NN-based reconstruction can enable rapid stiffness mapping for dynamic studies, functional imaging, and real-time clinical feedback.

title: [Generative artificial intelligence: a new tool for occupational health nurses].
desc: [Revue de l'infirmiere] Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is gradually being integrated into the practices of occupational health nurses. Based on a discussion session bringing together professionals from various sectors, this article analyzes their uses of AI in light of the scientific literature. The results show that AI primarily supports the planning of preventive measures and reflective practice, while reaffirming the central role of clinical judgment.

title: Explainability of genotype embedding models through observed cohort paths
desc: Deep learning models that combine genotypes with neuroimaging predict neurological diseases more accurately than either modality alone. Their clinical use, however, requires identifying which genetic variants a prediction is based on. Path-based attribution methods like Integrated Gradients address this by integrating the model's gradient from a baseline to the input. These methods assume the model accepts any point along that path as a valid input. Genotype models violate this assumption. They map the three discrete allele dosages \{0,1,2\} to vectors through a learned embedding defined only at those values, so a straight line passes through fractional genotypes at which no embedding, and therefore no gradient, exists. Attribution must therefore proceed in embedding space where the choice of path can affect the resulting attribution. We show that the commonly used per-variant estimator does not generally satisfy completeness. Additive separability guarantees completeness for this estimator, but interactions between variants generally break that property. Instead, we integrate along piecewise-linear embedding-space paths connecting genotype waypoints observed in the training cohort. Each path satisfies completeness in the continuum although the interiors of its segments are not necessarily observed. Our method improves faithfulness over Integrated Gradients and discretized Integrated Gradients under both perturbation protocols, achieves the strongest results for Parkinson's disease classification under support-preserving perturbations, and is competitive with a support-background Shapley baseline under per-variant perturbations. It also shows higher seed stability and better recovery of planted non-additive effects in a synthetic benchmark.

title: Learning inhibitor interactions from protein deep mutational scanning data and deep learning models.
source: PubMed · bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
desc: [bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology] Recent advances in protein language models, geometric deep learning, and structure prediction frameworks have the potential to accelerate computational drug discovery. However, it remains unclear how well these methods generalize beyond their training sets. Mutation-dependent drug responses present a challenge to these methods because there are often large effects from relatively small perturbations. Here, we systematically benchmark diverse mutational effect and drug-target affinity prediction models using deep mutational scanning datasets spanning 11 inhibitor conditions for the MET kinase domain. Across both mutational effect prediction and drug-target affinity tasks, current AI models produce largely ligand-invariant predictions despite experimentally distinct inhibitor-dependent fitness landscapes. Ligand-aware geometric models, including LigandMPNN and LASErMPNN, partially recover experimentally validated resistance-associated hotspots, highlighting the importance of explicitly modeling protein-ligand interactions and local structural flexibility. In contrast, deep learning affinity prediction models underestimate mutation-induced changes in binding affinity. This deficiency likely reflects mutation-invariant structural priors derived from co-folded structure prediction frameworks and the absence of mutation-conditioned supervision in current affinity datasets. Finally, we further extended our analysis to several kinase-inhibitor deep mutational scanning datasets and confirm the overall trends. Our findings suggest that a primary limitation in improving performance on this task lies in the scarcity of mutation-conditioned protein-ligand training data rather than model architecture alone.

title: GPU-Accelerated Secure Inference for Drug--Target Interaction Prediction
desc: Deep learning models that predict drug--target interactions (DTI) can speed up drug discovery, but the candidate drugs they score are valuable intellectual property that their owners cannot reveal. Secure multiparty computation (MPC) lets two servers compute a prediction on a secret-shared drug, without either server learning the drug. However, secure inference of deep models is slow. Non-linear operations require communication between the servers, and MPC arithmetic does not map naturally to GPUs. In this paper, we present our solution to Track~III of the iDASH 2026 privacy and security competition, which asked for fast two-party secure DTI inference on GPUs. Our solution is built on the co-design of MPC-friendly models and MPC protocols. On the model side, we design SlimDTA, a DTI model that reduces the operations on the secret drug, and in particular the non-linear operations that require communication. On the protocol side, we build a GPU framework that evaluates the linear layers with additive secret sharing and the non-linear layers with function secret sharing, including a custom CUDA kernel for the comparisons. Our solution won first place in the competition, at under 10,ms per prediction on average, and its secure predictions match the plaintext model to within 0.02%.

title: Expert-level localization of fine-grained cardiac structures across the transthoracic echocardiogram.
source: PubMed · medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
desc: [medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences] 1.Artificial intelligence models for echocardiography interpret studies without identifying the structures that support their outputs. We show that this spatial grounding does not emerge from the pretraining of current vision-language models. General-purpose and medical vision-language models and an open-vocabulary detector recalled 3% or fewer of cardiac structures and scored below a box that never sees the image. EchoLens, a detector trained on 5,912 expert-annotated structures and 4,219 Doppler signals from 136 patients, recalled 87% and localized structures as reliably as a blinded expert reader (box centre within the reference in 95.7% and 95.3% of cases). It covers 21 structures across 11 transthoracic views and 11 spectral Doppler signal types. In external data, two physicians judged 81- 92% of its detections correct across all 11 views, and it identified the Doppler signal type in 83% of frames. EchoLens provides the spatial layer that grounded echocardiographic interpretation requires.

title: QUBO-based feature selection for MRI undersampling pattern design
desc: We formulate undersampling mask design for Cartesian magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) as a feature subset selection problem. Each sampling line is represented by a binary feature indicating whether it is included in each candidate mask. Using candidate masks and their training-set evaluations, we estimate mutual information (MI) and conditional mutual information (CMI). These estimates and a sampling-count penalty define a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) model. The model is solved using simulated annealing and quantum annealing to determine a feature subset and its corresponding sampling mask. We assess the selected subsets on the test set through zero-filled reconstruction in Fourier undersampling simulations using fastMRI knee magnitude reference images, with patient-disjoint training and test sets. At all six tested target sampling rates from 15% to 40%, the resulting reconstructions have lower mean root mean square error than those obtained with four conventional sampling methods. They also have higher mean structural similarity than those obtained using univariate mutual-information ranking at all tested rates. These results support information-theoretic feature selection as an approach to MRI undersampling mask design under the tested zero-filled simulation settings.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Fellowship Leadership: Practical Applications for Recruitment, Education, and Program Management.
desc: [Open forum infectious diseases] Fellowship program directors (PDs) oversee a broad range of responsibilities spanning recruitment, education, mentorship, evaluation, scheduling, accreditation, and program administration. These activities require substantial time and coordination, often with limited resources. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers an opportunity to support PD workflows. In this review, we describe practical applications of AI in fellowship leadership using real-world examples from an Infectious Diseases fellowship program. Applications include recruitment marketing, applicant review and summarization, multilingual global health education, individualized board preparation, and scheduling optimization. We also discuss governance considerations and lessons from other industries that have successfully integrated AI into complex workflows. Artificial intelligence can expand the PD toolkit and support more efficient program management, potentially allowing greater focus on mentorship, education, and program development. Further evaluation is needed to assess its effects on efficiency, cost, educational outcomes, and recruitment.

title: Empirical Variational Bayes Factorization for Longitudinal Matrix Data
desc: Collecting high-dimensional data over time for multiple individuals is increasingly common in biomedical research, particularly in studies of disease progression or molecular time-course experiments. Often data are missing or the timepoints are irregularly spaced across individuals. There is a lack of flexible methodology to explore latent patterns of change over time and account for missing data. We propose an empirical variational Bayes (EVB) approach to factorize high-dimensional longitudinal data, in which the underlying factors have temporal correlation over time. The EVB approach is computationally efficient and accommodates flexible covariance structures over time with automatic determination of all hyper-parameters (including the underlying rank, i.e., number of factors). Simulations demonstrate that the approach captures the underlying signal more precisely than other strategies, and performs well with respect to missing data imputation under different scenarios. An application to a gene time-course data for multiple sclerosis treatment provides a factorization with interpretable components over time and improved imputation accuracy for missing data.

title: Accuracy and Readability of Large Language Model-Powered Artificial Intelligence Chatbot Responses for Correcting Common Misconceptions About Dyslexia.
source: PubMed · American journal of speech-language pathology
desc: [American journal of speech-language pathology] The purpose of this project was to evaluate the accuracy and readability of ChatGPT's responses to questions related to common misconceptions about dyslexia. Three content area experts independently rated the accuracy of ChatGPT's responses to five questions related to common misconceptions about dyslexia. Ratings were averaged across raters to derive an overall accuracy score for each response. ChatGPT's responses were also analyzed for length, reading time, reading ease, and reading level. The overall accuracy of ChatGPT's responses was high. However, without additional prompting to adjust the length and/or reading level, ChatGPT's responses were written for advanced readers and took up to 2 min to read. This study provides preliminary evidence that, at present, ChatGPT may be a useful tool for procuring scientifically valid information about dyslexia. Limitations and future directions are discussed.

title: Disentangling Monitor Hardware Artifacts and Smoothing Lag for Shift-Robust Intraoperative EEG and Hemodynamic Risk Calibration
desc: Commercial intraoperative electroencephalography (EEG) and blood pressure monitors introduce cyclic impedance pulses, smoothing delays, direct-current (DC) drift, and cuff holds that confound risk forecasting and uncertainty calibration. We developed a causal signal-conditioning and shift-robust conformal calibration framework across 5,439 public anesthesia procedures. Streaming filters blank 10.13-min 64-Hz impedance checks, apply unclipped post-notch conditioning, separate 63-s suppression-ratio lag, and distinguish three-channel cuff inflations from dropouts across propofol-remifentanil total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA; N = 3,214), volatile anesthesia (N = 2,046), European endoscopy sedation (N = 171), and DC-coupled surgery (N = 8). De-impedanced cortical tree ensembles were compared against deep sequence models, paired with patient-cluster Subgroup-Covariate-Weighted Conformal Risk Control (CRC) and lag-buffered online Conformal Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) tracking. Pre-filter blanking removed 97.90% and 97.60% of false flatline conflicts while preserving 99.23% and 98.96% of deep suppression. On unseen TIVA surgeries (N = 525), cortical features achieved area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) 0.3135 (1.94% prevalence) and 0.1627 (0.82% lag-free prevalence), with no detectable difference from deep encoders (p >= 0.36) and no cortical gain for hypotension (0.3432 vs. 0.3437, p = 0.784). Zero-retraining volatile transfer (N = 1,048) showed no detectable difference from an end-tidal gas oracle on lag-free suppression (0.0820 vs. 0.0736, p = 0.472). Subgroup-Covariate-Weighted CRC bounded all 70 TIVA shift cells at <= 4.38% (alpha = 5.0%) in 66.32 ms per 30-s epoch. Causal artifact disentangling and shift-aware conformal calibration support reliable real-time intraoperative risk bounds within explicit physiological observability limits.

title: Large Language Model-Enhanced Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Enterprise Workflow Orchestration via Graph Semantic Routing.
source: PubMed · Journal of visualized experiments : JoVE
desc: [Journal of visualized experiments : JoVE] Automated orchestration of enterprise workflows is a core technical challenge in digital transformation, and predefined rule templates adapt poorly once business scenarios change frequently. This work proposes LeMARLA, a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) architecture enhanced by a large language model (LLM). An LLM-driven decomposition module parses natural language business instructions into a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of subtasks and re-decomposes the affected subgraph whenever execution feedback reports a failure. A graph attention network-based semantic routing module computes task-employee matching on a heterogeneous graph of tasks, employees, and skills. A MARL module learns a global coordination policy under centralized training with decentralized execution, and the routing matching scores enter the policy logits as a differentiable semantic prior, so routing and policy are optimized along a single path rather than in sequence. In a log-replay evaluation parameterized by twelve months of real enterprise workflow records, LeMARLA reached a task completion rate of 91.7%, an end-to-end latency of 30.4 min, a load balance index of 0.71 per minute and a routing accuracy at rank three of 82.6%, outperforming all eight baselines with a Holm-corrected p value below 0.001 over ten independent runs and exceeding the logged historical assignment by 3.2 percentage points of completion rate and 26.2% of latency, with gains of 3.7 percentage points and 30.3% against the simulator replay of that same assignment. Ablations quantified the contribution of each module, decomposition quality was measured against an annotated reference set, and performance remained stable up to 2,000 employees.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven sustainable polymers research: a lifecycle-integrated perspective.
desc: [Materials horizons] The transition toward sustainable polymers necessitates coordinated optimization across the entire materials life cycle. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are increasingly deployed to accelerate polymer discovery, yet progress in molecular design, processing and recycling is commonly assessed within individual stages. This review critically examines the shift from single-stage property prediction toward a lifecycle-integrated AI framework. We consider five interconnected dimensions-feedstock, processing, use-phase, end-of-life and system-level impacts-and evaluate the data and model outputs that link them. Representative studies reveal how polymer structure and processing history shape recovery pathways, how manufacturing results feed back into formulation design, and how predicted reaction yields enter process balances and environmental and economic assessment. We distinguish single-stage prediction, sequential coupling, feedback-guided multi-stage optimization and optimization incorporating life cycle assessment (LCA) and techno-economic analysis (TEA), assessing the evidence for progress from laboratory demonstrations toward scalable implementation. Finally, we identify priorities in polymer data, experimental feedback, uncertainty propagation and laboratory-to-plant transfer for advancing AI-enabled circular polymer development.

title: Integrating Generative Artificial Intelligence-Based Concept Mapping to Enhance Nursing Students' Critical Thinking, Cognitive Load, and Self-Efficacy.
desc: [Computers, informatics, nursing : CIN] Entrustable professional activities are important for training nursing students and enhancing their abilities to manage and care for pregnant women through clinical case studies. This study explored a generative artificial intelligence (AI)-based concept mapping (CM) approach within this framework to improve nursing students' learning outcomes in obstetrics education, focusing on critical thinking, cognitive load, and self-efficacy. Using a quasi-experimental design with pre-test and post-test evaluations, this study compared the effects of an AI-based CM activity with a conventional CM method. Results showed the AI-based approach significantly reduced cognitive load and improved students' critical thinking and self-efficacy. This innovative method demonstrated potential as an effective teaching strategy in nursing education. Nursing educators could incorporate such technologies to better support students' development in entrustable professional activities.

title: Research progress and prospects of cochlear implant technology.
desc: [Frontiers in neuroscience] Traditional cochlear implant systems depend on external devices and face challenges related to convenience, esthetics, and auditory performance in complex soundscapes. Recently, research has shifted from "functional substitution" to "functional enhancement" and "biological fusion." However, most emerging approaches remain in the preclinical, prototype verification, or early clinical stages, lacking substantial evidence of clinical benefits. This narrative review examines research progress across five key dimensions of cochlear implants: The electrode interface has advanced from passive implants to dynamic, adaptive, and biologically active intelligent interfaces. Signal processing strategies are moving toward intelligence and physiological adaptation, with deep learning primarily used for noise suppression and coding optimization; however, clinical application is limited by real-time performance and individual variability. Bionic sensing aims to replicate the energy conversion mechanism between hair cells and the basement membrane at the signal source, currently focusing on laboratory prototypes. Optogenetics-driven optical regulation offers high spatial selectivity but remains in the early preclinical stage. The development of fully implanted systems emphasizes internal energy supply, ultra-low power consumption processing, and system integration, marking a significant engineering direction for making devices "invisible." Each section of this article critically evaluates evidence maturity and transformation barriers, highlighting common challenges such as long-term biological stability, safety, energy consumption, and regulatory verification that must be addressed before large-scale clinical application. Future advancements will require collaboration among materials science, neuroscience, microelectronics, and artificial intelligence to create a two-way high-fidelity interface. The ultimate goal is not only to restore hearing but also to reconstruct a more natural auditory perception.

title: A Hybrid Large Language Model and Diffusion Framework for Rational Promoter Design.
desc: [ACS synthetic biology] High-performance promoters are essential tools for precisely regulating gene expression, yet their rational design within the vast combinatorial sequence space remains a major challenge. Here, we present a hybrid framework that integrates a large language model (LLM) with a diffusion model to enable data-driven and interpretable promoter design. The fine-tuned LLM predicts promoter strength with high accuracy and, through systematic sequence mutations, identifies biologically essential core regions. A diffusion model is then conditioned on these core regions to reconstruct non-core regions and generate complete promoter sequences. We experimentally validated this approach in Escherichia coli by high-throughput barcoded promoter activity sequencing: 7.78% of the designed promoters outperformed the benchmark promoter BBa_J23119, with the best variants reaching approximately 2.5-fold the expression level of BBa_J23119. By explicitly coupling interpretability with generative design, this strategy provides a practical framework for promoter design in E. coli and may be adaptable to other regulatory sequence engineering tasks.

title: DAQplugin: Interactive deep learning-based validation of Cryo-EM protein models in ChimeraX.
desc: [Structure (London, England : 1993)] Although protein structures are increasingly determined by cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM), structure modeling frequently suffers from residue misassignments and sequence register shifts, particularly in regions with ambiguous density. Here, we present DAQplugin, a ChimeraX plugin for real-time evaluation of protein models against cryo-EM density maps using the deep-learning-based residue-wise model quality (DAQ) score. Unlike existing validation tools applied after model construction, DAQplugin enables interactive validation during model building and refinement. DAQ identifies residue assignment errors, including sequence register shifts, as well as local conformational modeling errors. DAQplugin also guides correction of sequence register shifts by suggesting alternative residue placements along the backbone. The plugin is computationally efficient and runs on standard CPUs without requiring GPU hardware, enabling deep-learning-based validation on ordinary laptops during interactive model building, model-map fitting, and refinement. DAQplugin facilitates more accurate interpretation of cryo-EM density maps and improves the reliability assessment of protein structure models.

title: TALQ: A reproducible language model questionnaire for dense measurement of depressive and anxious states.
source: PubMed · medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
desc: [medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences] Depression and anxiety are often assessed weeks or months apart with brief questionnaires covering few symptoms, leaving changes between assessments unobserved. Here, we introduce TALQ, a scoring system in which a large language model rates 52 symptoms from text, and use it to score 491 members of two online mental health communities every two weeks for a year. Ratings were stable across samples, predicted human annotations of interpersonal risk factors, low self-esteem and depression severity, and agreed with inventories completed by the same model. The scores mapped into 12 replicable symptom factors, including fearful preoccupation and social strain. Sleep disturbance and self-harm content consistently preceded overwhelm and emotional pain, respectively, two weeks later. People differed mainly in the states they occupied rather than transitions between them, and 13% entered in a crisis that remitted over months. Overall, our findings suggest that TALQ can measure expressed mental states densely and quantify longitudinal dynamics.

title: CryoID2: deep learning-enhanced identification of protein and RNA from cryoEM maps.
source: PubMed · bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
desc: [bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology] Identifying the molecular components of cryoEM/cryoET maps of endogenous or poorly characterized complexes remains a major bottleneck. CryoID2 addresses this by integrating deep learning-based feature prediction with sequence prioritization and structural evaluation. Three 3D U-Nets extract structure classes, key-atom positions, and reduced residue/nucleotide types from the input map. These predictions support backbone tracing and the generation of short sequence queries that rank candidates from a user-supplied pool-using BLASTp for proteins and a maximin strategy for RNA. Corresponding PDB or AlphaFold models are then retrieved, rigidly fitted using predicted features and experimental density, and ranked by map agreement. Module-level tests show high-recall feature prediction and resolution-dependent atom clustering, while a 52-case benchmark recovers near-reference fitting quality. In practice, cryoID2 correctly identified PfA-M17 from a 166-protein mass-spectrometry pool and the unannotated Ca-raiA RNA from a genome-derived non-coding sequence set, demonstrating a unified sequence-plus-structure route to molecular identification in cryoEM maps.

title: Consensus modeling of sex hormone-binding globulin binding using machine learning and deep learning approaches.
desc: [Frontiers in chemistry] Sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG) regulates the bioavailability of circulating androgens and estrogens through high-affinity binding. Chemicals that bind SHBG may alter the equilibrium between bound and free hormone fractions, making SHBG binding activity a relevant endpoint for endocrine disruption assessment. However, experimental assessment of SHBG binding is resource intensive with low throughput, limiting its application to large chemical inventories. To enable large-scale screening, we developed machine learning, deep learning, and consensus models using a dataset of 125 chemicals tested in a human SHBG competitive binding assay. Random forest, support vector machine, and multilayer perceptron models were trained using molecular descriptors, while a graph isomorphism network with edge features was trained using molecular graph representations. A consensus model was then generated by averaging the predicted probabilities from the four individual models. Model performance was evaluated using 100 iterations of 5-fold cross-validation and external validation with an independent dataset curated from ChEMBL. All models showed good predictive performance, with accuracy ranging from 0.811 to 0.855 in internal validation and from 0.793-0.890 in external validation. The consensus model had the best overall performance, yielding accuracy of 0.855 and 0.884 in internal and external validations, respectively. Confidence analysis further showed that prediction accuracy increased with prediction confidence, indicating the practical utility of confidence estimates for decision-making. These results indicate that consensus modeling can reliably predict SHBG-binding activity and provide a rapid, cost-effective approach for screening large chemical inventories. The proposed models can support the prioritization of chemicals for experimental testing, facilitate the identification of potential endocrine-disrupting substances, and complement New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) used in chemical safety assessment.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence-Driven Financial Decision Support: A Hybrid Cost-Sensitive Stacking Framework for Bankruptcy Risk Assessment.
source: PubMed · Journal of visualized experiments : JoVE
desc: [Journal of visualized experiments : JoVE] Predicting bankruptcy risk plays a critical role in enterprise risk management and capital structure optimization by allowing the identification of bankruptcy risks in advance before financial degradation happens. However, traditional financial decision support systems suffer from class imbalance, data leakage, poor generalization, and limited model interpretability, leading to inaccurate minority-class predictions. For this reason, this research proposes an innovative generative AI-driven financial decision support system called the generative cost-sensitive stacking ensemble (GCS-SE) framework. The proposed framework combines four approaches, namely generative models, cost-sensitive learning, hybrid ensemble classification, and explainable artificial intelligence in a single leakage-safe framework. First, financial data records undergo pre-processing via a leakage-aware pre-processing pipeline involving outlier treatment and feature scaling. Then, a conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) is used to find out how minority classes are distributed in bankruptcy data and generate realistic synthetic financial data to mitigate the issue of class imbalance and maintain the financial properties. Next, a heterogeneous ensemble comprising XGBoost, random forest, logistic regression, and light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM) is trained on the balanced dataset based on a cost-sensitive learning strategy. Additionally, the Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) approach is applied to interpret features and facilitate more informed financial decision-making. According to experiments performed on the Taiwan Bankruptcy Prediction dataset, the proposed GCS-SE framework achieves an ROC-AUC of 96.83%, a PR-AUC of 93.14%, a precision of 88.22%, a recall of 86.08%, an F1-score of 87.14%, an accuracy of 92.38%, and an MCC of 0.8173, demonstrating strong discriminative performance for imbalanced bankruptcy prediction. Thus, it can be concluded that the suggested methodology shows promise as a tool for capital structure optimization and bankruptcy risk assessment.

title: Artificial intelligence raises operational carbon emissions from data centers.
desc: [Environmental science and ecotechnology] Artificial intelligence is expanding computing demand, yet how this expansion affects the operational carbon emissions that arise from purchased electricity at data centers remains poorly quantified. Existing work has not systematically isolated this operational-phase outcome or examined the mechanisms, thresholds, and spatial patterns that shape it. Here we show that artificial intelligence development raises operational carbon emissions from data centers. A bottom-up accounting of 1090 data centers across 162 cities in China from 2015 to 2024 indicates that a one-standard-deviation increase in a multidimensional artificial-intelligence index is associated with an additional 68.82 million tonnes of these emissions. Local green data-center policies and higher inter-city green-technology cooperation both weaken the positive association once they exceed estimated thresholds, but neither reverses it. Spatial spillovers are non-monotonic, negative between roughly 150 and 650 km and positive at longer distances. The results identify the conditions under which artificial-intelligence growth elevates operational emissions from computing infrastructure.

title: Improving real-time search through deep learning-enhanced fragment ion indexing.
source: PubMed · bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
desc: [bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology] The fragment ion indexed database searching approach enables highly efficient tandem mass spectrometry database searches, including real-time search workflows. However, the index can require tens of gigabytes of memory, often exceeding the free memory available on instrument acquisition computers running the search. This restricts the size of the searchable database, the variable modification space, and the number of searches that can run concurrently. To address this problem, we developed an index-pruning pipeline within the Comet database search tool using Carafe, a deep learning tool that predicts fragment ion intensities based on peptide sequences. In our approach, only fragment ion positions that are predicted to be observable are written in the index, eliminating entries that are unlikely to contribute to spectrum detection. We evaluated this approach on two search spaces in three index configurations to demonstrate that masking significantly reduced the number of fragment ion index entries and, consequently, peak search memory use. Masked searches were also faster than unmasked searches and identified a comparable number of peptide-spectrum matches. Because all prediction and masking steps are performed before searching, their cost is amortized across repeated, future searches of the same database and modification configuration, introducing no per-spectrum search overhead. The complete implementation is open source with an Apache license.

title: Rollout models of human planning with exact action probabilities.
desc: [PLoS computational biology] One proposed mechanism for human planning is the mental simulation, or "rollout," of potential action sequences to evaluate future outcomes. While rollout-based models have seen great success in artificial intelligence, cognitive models that describe how people use rollouts remain scarce, in part because they are difficult to fit to behavioral data. Existing methods rely on computationally intensive simulations that result in approximate, noisy estimates of latent planning parameters. We introduce ROSETTE (Rollouts with Stochastic Early Termination and Tractable Estimation), a rollout-based model for finite goal-directed tasks with absorbing goals that provides analytically tractable, simulation-free model fitting. ROSETTE treats planning as a sequence of mental simulations formalized as an absorbing Markov chain. The model deterministically accumulates analytically computed expected rollout evidence and performs a variable number of policy-update cycles. We fit ROSETTE to data from human participants in two multi-step planning tasks and found that it well accounted for a rich set of summary statistics of behavior. By making this specific class of absorbing-goal rollout models tractable, our framework provides a testable account of how people may simulate and evaluate possible futures.

title: Unsupervised Selective Labeling for Semi-Supervised Aerial Imagery Recognition.
desc: [Ecology and evolution] Traditional aerial wildlife monitoring surveys rely on rapid visual identification and counting by expert biologists from moving aircraft. Modern camera systems mounted on survey aircraft are now being deployed to collect large datasets of imagery that provide a persistent, reusable snapshot of wildlife populations. Manual analysis of these extensive datasets can overwhelm the staffing of natural resource agencies, especially for large-scale surveys. Deep learning systems are being investigated as a potential solution to automate analysis, but significant human effort is still required to curate a labeled dataset for model training. To address this challenge, we propose Semi-Supervised Aerial Imagery Recognition (referred to as SSAR), a framework that minimizes annotation effort while maintaining classification performance. The key of SSAR is to select the best subset of images for annotation while leveraging the hidden information from the remaining unlabeled data. Concretely, SSAR integrates three components: (1) unsupervised feature learning tailored to aerial imagery to capture ecologically meaningful visual patterns, (2) unsupervised selective labeling that prioritizes representative and diverse images for annotation, and (3) semi-supervised classification that incorporates the remaining unlabeled images during training. We evaluate SSAR on wildlife recognition case studies using object-centric image crops from high-resolution aerial imagery collected over the United States Atlantic Outer Continental Shelf (OCS) and the Great Lakes region, comprising 57,265 images across 11 coarse categories. Using only 6.4% labeled data, SSAR matches the fully supervised macro accuracy of 85.0% achieved with 100% labeled data and further surpasses it by reaching 86.8% with 12.8% labeled data. These results demonstrate that SSAR enables accurate and scalable aerial wildlife recognition with an order-of-magnitude reduction in manual annotation.
